name: Soft Ginger Cake
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: brown sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a cupful of brown sugar

ingredients.name: more cupfuls of sifted flour
ingredients.originalText: two more cupfuls of sifted flour

instructions.text: Stir to a cream one cupful of butter and half a cupful of brown sugar.
Add to this two cupfuls of cooking molasses, a cupful of sweet milk, a tablespoonful of ginger, a teaspoonful of ground cinnamon.
Add three eggs, the whites and yolks beaten separately.
Beat into this two cups of sifted flour.
Add a teaspoonful of soda dissolved in a spoonful of water and last, two more cupfuls of sifted flour.
Butter and paper two common square bread-pans.
Divide the mixture and pour half into each.
Bake in a moderate oven from forty to sixty minutes. If sour milk is used the cakes are much lighter, but either sweet or sour is most excellent.

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stir to a cream one cupful of butter and half a cupful of brown sugar.
2. Add to this two cupfuls of cooking molasses, a cupful of sweet milk, a tablespoonful of ginger, a teaspoonful of ground cinnamon.
3. Beat all thoroughly together.
4. Add three eggs, the whites and yolks beaten separately.
5. Beat into this two cups of sifted flour.
6. Add a teaspoonful of soda dissolved in a spoonful of water and last, two more cupfuls of sifted flour.
7. Butter and paper two common square bread-pans.
8. Divide the mixture and pour half into each.
9. Bake in a moderate oven from forty to sixty minutes. If sour milk is used the cakes are much lighter, but either sweet or sour is most excellent.
